name: Lacuna — Experience Archive Platform
description: Lacuna is a curated neural-recording platform where users upload, tag, and share full sensory experiences — meals, skyline views from Spire terraces, the texture of black market chrome being installed, the specific exhaustion of a double shift in a Tier 2 fabrication hall. Founded in 2196 by Soraya Nkemdirim-Vasquez as a reaction against the ephemerality of Pulse, Lacuna operates on a permanent archive model where experiences are stored indefinitely and can be licensed, remixed, or sold. The platform has become the de facto cultural memory of GLMZ, with curators — called Archivists — who organize experiences into navigable collections. Corponation Helixar AG quietly purchased a 40% stake in 2214 without public disclosure.
cultural_impact: Lacuna has created a thriving economy around experience-as-commodity, with professional 'Sensorialists' who live deliberately interesting lives solely to sell their recordings — a new creative class that blurs the line between artist, performer, and product.
key_figures: Cato Reinholt-Eze (lead Archivist, Shelf Experience Collection)
locations: The Gutter Collection server farm, Shelf Ward 12
Sensorialist Row, Tier 3 arts district near the Milwaukee Spur
story_hooks: A Lacuna experience tagged as a routine Tier 2 commute contains a three-second fragment that proves a corponation security team committed a covered-up massacre — the uploader has no idea it's in there
An anonymous Archivist is assembling a collection called 'Last Hours' — experiences uploaded by people who died within 24 hours of their recording — and someone is commissioning it obsessively

Soraya Nkemdirim-Vasquez discovers the extent of Helixar's ownership and begins a quiet campaign to reclaim the platform, recruiting Sensorialists to a coordinated archive migration that could crash Lacuna's valuation overnight
user_base: 1.8 million registered users, 340,000 active monthly uploaders; primary demographic is Tier 2-3 creative and service workers aged 22-45
monetization: Experience licensing fees, Archivist subscription tiers, corporate bulk-purchase of demographic experience sets for market research, Sensorialist creator revenue share
notable_feature: The Gutter Collection — a sub-archive of exclusively Shelf-origin experiences maintained by volunteer Archivists as a counter-record to the platform's Tier 3-skewed curation, considered the most historically significant body of work on the platform
